best_field_traits: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.
Introduced cultivated cereal, generally annual with fibrous roots rather than a perennial knotty rhizome.
Stout erect stems and comparatively broad foliage, often around 6–20 mm wide.
Dense heavy terminal foxtail head, often about 5–30 cm long; shape varies with cultivated form.
Bristles are modified sterile branchlets below spikelets, not grass floret awns.
Field plant may reflect selected cultivars/hybrids; species concept and origin distinguish it from indigenous bristlegrasses.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Same plant entire root/base, broad blades and heavy terminal panicle with ruler
Subtending 1–3 persistent bristles attached to mature spikelet under 10–20×, with 1-mm scale
Upper fertile floret and lower glumes at 10–20× for escaped foxtail millet vs green foxtail
True leaf collar ligule, sheath hair bases, and fruiting head at different ages
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Cultivated/escaped S. italica is annual and often has conspicuously thick, sometimes lobed heads; S. parviflora has short knotty rhizomes and usually 4–12 bristles per spikelet, S. reverchonii a slender often interrupted head and sparse bristles, and S. scheelei a longer, more open/tapered head with usually solitary long projecting bristles. S. viridis is another ANNUAL look-alike outside the installed set; head bulk alone doesn't establish crop identity.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Cultivated/escaped ANNUAL with fibrous roots and a dense, sometimes lobed or nodding foxtail head; inspect a mature spikelet's persistent subtending BRISTLES (sterile branches), not awns. Compare the point of spikelet disarticulation with green foxtail; head bulk alone is not a diagnosis.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Erect annual up to approximately 1.5 m, without knotty rhizomes; blades commonly 6–20 mm wide in WFO regional treatments. Ligule 1–3 mm, a fringed membrane or short hair fringe (WFO; Go Botany 1–2 mm). No auricles. Verify true blade/sheath junction rather than nearby sheath-mouth hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_inflorescence_and_bristles: Dense spike-like, sometimes lobed panicle approximately 6–40 cm long (cultivar-variable). Spikelets about 2–3(–3.5) mm. FNA-derived canonical genus lesson gives usually 1–3 bristles, up to ~12 mm; other regional floras describe 2–5 bristles up to 15–16 mm. Count intact attachments and label the regional variation rather than treating one count as absolute.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_spikelet_glumes_lemmas_awns: Two florets: lower sterile or staminate, upper fertile. Lower glume ~1/3–1/2 spikelet length, 1–3-veined; upper glume ~2/3 to nearly spikelet-length, 5–7(–9)-veined. Lower sterile lemma near spikelet-length, ~5-veined, palea absent/reduced; upper fertile lemma indurated, smooth to faintly rugulose, ~2–3 mm. No true lemma or glume awns; persistent basal bristles are sterile branchlets.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: S. viridis is also annual and can resemble smaller cultivated millet; compare disarticulation (italica florets above more persistent glumes versus viridis often below spikelet). Native S. parviflora has short hard knotty rhizomes and generally 4–12 bristles per spikelet; S. reverchonii is slender and interrupted with sparse 2–8-mm bristles; S. scheelei has long 10–35-mm projecting bristles.
last_mile_photo_holds: Same rooted identified annual with complete head and centimeter ruler; no inference of cultivar or provenance from a single image.
At least three mature spikelets at 10–20× with 1-mm scale showing actual bristle origin/count, glumes, sterile lemma and fertile lemma.
True 1–3-mm ligule and collar from the same identified plant, with sheath-mouth hairs separately marked.
Same-scale S. viridis comparison demonstrating real disarticulation and S. parviflora rooted rhizome comparison.

items.why_it_matters: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.

items.label: Reverchon's bristlegrass — interrupted slender panicle
items.image_role: Existing Texas source-labelled photo for sparse panicle architecture, not measured bristle anatomy
items.caption: Eric Knight's photo shows a narrow vertical seedhead with separated, sparse clusters of green spikelets. The finger is only an informal size cue. The tiny spikelet bases do not resolve the number or exact length of persistent bristles.
items.why_it_matters: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.

items.why_it_matters: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Foxtail millet — examine the ligule, bristle insertion and two-floret spikelet
steps: START with real SOURCE-LABELLED LIGULE photo 2: locate actual blade/sheath junction; distinguish the membranous or hair-fringed ligule from surrounding sheath mouth hairs. Source photo is unmeasured, so do not estimate length from pixels.

OPEN real SOURCE-ANNOTATED SPIKELET photo 3: identify the two glumes and upper hardened fertile floret before studying the bristles. Original author annotations are source content; do not claim our own pixel-certified arrows.

ON AN ATTACHED MATURE SPIKELET, inspect the persistent subtending bristles: these are sterile branchlets BELOW the spikelet, NOT lemma awns. Count actual insertions across several spikelets (described ranges vary).

RETURN to photo 1 for the dense heavy often nodding crop head and relatively broad leaves. These support a cultivated annual foxtail millet hypothesis but do not independently prove species or cultivar.

COMPARE the three existing different-species gallery panels: S. parviflora reproductive close-up (index 3), S. reverchonii interrupted slender head (index 4), and S. scheelei long projecting bristles (index 5). None demonstrates a connected rooted rhizomatous plant; photograph the actual perennial rootstock separately.

CRITICAL missing paired diagnostic: same-voucher mature S. italica and annual S. viridis spikelets showing true disarticulation and bristle attachment with a 1-mm ruler. Crop forms can look similar; leave Setaria sp. when unresolved.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Avoid native/introduced calls or true species ID solely from bristle silhouette. Count several attached mature spikelets and study rootstock on the same plant.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · ANNUAL MILLET, HEAVY HEAD
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: stout annual with broad leaves and a dense, often lobed or nodding crop-like foxtail head
field_id_short_tiles.details: Introduced cultivated/escaped annual, often 30–150 cm tall, blades commonly 6–20 mm wide. Cultivar-dependent panicles may be about 6–40 cm, often heavy and variably lobed. Check fibrous annual roots and absence of perennial knotty rhizomes rather than calling species from head bulk alone. Existing photo shows head architecture, not a connected rooted voucher.
field_id_short_tiles.status: WHOLE HEAD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Look inside the blade–sheath junction for a 1–3 mm fringed membrane or hair fringe
field_id_short_tiles.details: World Flora Online gives about 1–3 mm; Go Botany gives 1–2 mm. Separate the true ligule from hairs at the sheath mouth; no auricles. Existing physically archived Stefan.lefnaer collar photograph shows the source-labelled organ, but a millimeter-calibrated Texas specimen has not been verified.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL COLLAR PHOTO — MEASURED LOCAL LIGULE NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · BRISTLES ARE NOT AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Count persistent basal bristles below a ripe spikelet; regional sources differ on 1–3 versus 2–5
field_id_short_tiles.details: North Central Texas key generally describes 1–3 persistent bristles, while WFO/AusGrass regional treatments allow 2–5, up to about 15–16 mm. These are sterile reduced branches, not glume or lemma awns. Count several attached mature spikelets with a 1-mm ruler; no existing photograph independently resolves the exact bristle origin and count.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE GLUMES ON A MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelets about 2–3.5 mm; lower glume roughly 1/3–1/2, upper usually ~2/3 to nearly spikelet length
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lower glume commonly 1–3-veined; upper glume 5–7(–9)-veined. Published upper-glume proportions differ between floras and cultivated forms. The physically archived source-annotated spikelet photograph teaches organ location but does not verify Texas measurements or author labels independently. No glume awns.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-ANNOTATED SPIKELET — CALIBRATED GLUME MACRO NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE STERILE AND FERTILE LEMMAS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma near spikelet length; upper fertile lemma hardened, about 2–3 mm, smooth to finely wrinkled
field_id_short_tiles.details: Spikelet typically has a lower sterile/staminate and upper fertile floret. Lower lemma often 5–7-veined, lower palea absent or small in regional descriptions. Upper fertile lemma indurated, shiny to finely rugulose; no long lemma awn. With mature material check the disarticulation ABOVE the glumes; do not infer the break point from an intact picture.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE ANATOMY — BREAK POINT NOT VERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · DON'T CONFUSE IT WITH NATIVE FOXTAILS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Distinguish annual millet from knotroot, Reverchon's and southwestern bristlegrasses using roots and ripe bristle attachments
field_id_short_tiles.details: Three REAL different-species comparison panels already exist: panel 4 (zero-based 3) shows S. parviflora's reproductive bristles, panel 5 (index 4) shows S. reverchonii's slender interrupted head, and panel 6 (index 5) shows S. scheelei's longer projecting bristles. Panel 1 (index 0) is the introduced S. italica crop head. These images support visual comparisons but do NOT show connected perennial rhizomes or calibrated same-stage mature bristle insertion. S. parviflora has perennial knotty rhizomes and commonly 4–12 bristles; S. reverchonii has a slender interrupted head with sparse bristles; S. scheelei has long conspicuous usually solitary bristles. Annual S. viridis remains an UNPHOTOGRAPHED close look-alike; verify mature disarticulation and fertile lemma texture rather than identifying crop escape by head bulk.
field_id_short_tiles.status: THREE REAL LOOK-ALIKE PANELS LINKED — ROOTED AND MATURE-SPIKELET COMPARISONS STILL NEEDED
